coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Season
You Didn't Choose
coverDek: For the plus-one you don't have, the questions at every holiday table, and the ache of a chapter that hasn't started yet — five prayers for the single season nobody else can see from the outside.

points.hook: Lord, I'm not where I pictured I'd be by now, and I feel it every time another invitation says plus-one.
paragraphs: There's a particular quiet that comes with being the one still single at the table, watching a group chat fill up with engagement rings and nursery photos while your own news stays the same. I'm learning that waiting isn't the same as being forgotten, and that my life isn't paused just because this chapter hasn't started. Lord, teach me to live fully in the season I'm actually in, not the one I keep rehearsing in my head.
points.verseText: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

points.hook: I decree: I am not incomplete because I am unmarried.
paragraphs: I decree over my life tonight: singleness is not a diagnosis and it is not a deficiency — in the name of Jesus, I reject every voice that has made me feel like a project waiting to be finished! My Maker calls Himself my husband in this season, and I will not let a wedding date define a worth He already settled at the cross.
points.verseText: For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name.

points.hook: Notice what another engagement post just did to your shoulders.
paragraphs: Notice what happened in your body when you saw that announcement again — the tightening in your chest, the breath you held without meaning to. That reaction isn't shameful, it's human; longing lives in the body as much as the heart. Before you scroll past it and pretend it didn't land, let the Lord meet you in that exact tightness and remind you that you are fearfully and wonderfully made, fully, right now, not someday.
points.verseText: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.

points.hook: Somebody at church stopped coming because every sermon illustration assumed they were already married.
paragraphs: Family, somebody in this church is quietly pulling away because they've heard one too many messages that only had marriage and children in mind, and they felt like a footnote in their own house of worship. You are not a project for the married couples to pray over and fix — you are a full member of this body, with gifts the church needs today, not after a wedding.
points.verseText: For as we have many members in one body... so we, being many, are one body in Christ.

points.hook: Child, I am not withholding — I am building something you can't see yet.
paragraphs: Child, I know the nights you've asked Me why everyone else's story seems to be moving and yours feels stuck on the same page. I am not withholding good from you, and I have never forgotten the desires I planted in your own heart. I know the thoughts I think toward you, and not one of them was designed to leave you waiting forever.
points.verseText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named the season you're in, don't let silence turn into shame — come back tomorrow for the next series.
